credentials.description: Intron API key (Authorization: Bearer); every call hits production

example_prompt: Turn a short Wolof or Hausa text into speech and get the audio file location in the same response.

text.description: the text to process. The page says 'less than or equal to 4096 characters'; see gotchas for the lower limits in the documented 400s.

voice_accent.description: Accent for the speech voice. Must be listed for the chosen voice_language — af (Afrikaans): afrikaans; am (Amharic): amharic; en (English): afrikaans, hausa, igbo, luganda, sepedi, swahili, setswana, xhosa, yoruba, zulu; ha (Hausa): hausa; ig (Igbo): igbo; rw (Kinyarwanda): kinyarwanda; lg (Luganda): luganda; om (Oromo): oromo; pcm (Pidgin): pidgin; sn (Shona): shona; sw (Swahili): swahili; wo (Wolof): wolof; yo (Yoruba): yoruba. Source: https://docs.voice.intron.io/docs/tts/supported-languages-and-accents (snapshot 2026-10-24, sha256 0ac43d23555e2e428e27f242e84890443624f316811c308cf9c88c0625821e3f); every accent is listed with 'male,female'.

voice_gender.description: Voice gender (options 'male / female'; the docs' description repeats 'Accent for the speech voice'). Every listed accent has male and female voices.

output_audio_format.description: Specify the output audio format. The docs list WAV (.wav) and OPUS (.opus) and give 'wav' as the default; the value 'opus' is inferred from that table, not written in the docs.

audio_path.description: Location of the generated audio (documented example: "http://myaudio.wav"). Lifetime and download auth are not documented.

processing_status.description: Values listed on the Get Text Status page.

text_id.description: Present only in the documented 503 timeout body; pass it to get_speech_synthesis_status.

status.description: "Ok" in the documented examples, including the 503 timeout body.

message.description: e.g. "invalid text voice accent,{accent} not supported for language {language}".

gotchas: The API key comes from the developers tab of your account on voice.intron.io; send it as 'Authorization: Bearer {key}' from your backend only — the docs say never expose it in client-side code.
The body is JSON and the header table requires 'Content-Type: application/json' — send it, even though the docs' JavaScript samples omit it.
Character limit is contradictory: the page says 'less than or equal to 4096 characters', but the documented 400 says 'max limit of 100 characters'. Keep text short or split it.

voice_accent must be listed for voice_language ('invalid text voice accent,{accent} not supported for language {language}') and voice_gender for voice_accent ('invalid text voice gender,{gender} not supported for accent {accent}'), both 400. English (en) takes the accents afrikaans, hausa, igbo, luganda, sepedi, swahili, setswana, xhosa, yoruba, zulu; every other language takes only its own. On this page the Hausa JavaScript sample sends voice_language 'ha' with voice_accent 'swahili', which the table does not list for 'ha' (cURL and Python send 'hausa') — follow the table.
TTS covers 13 voice languages — af, am, en, ha, ig, rw, lg, om, pcm, sn, sw, wo, yo — fewer than speech-to-text: no French and no Fulani/Pulaar voice.

The request can time out after 120 seconds with HTTP 503. The docs say the text_id in the 503 response can be used with get_speech_synthesis_status; the documented 503 body is {"data":{"text_id":...},"message":"tts text queued for processing","status":"Ok"} — status "Ok" despite the 503.
The success response carries no text_id: only audio_duration_in_seconds, audio_path and processing_status.
audio_path is the generated audio's location (example "http://myaudio.wav"). How long it stays valid and whether downloading it needs the API key are not documented — download it promptly.
The documented 400 for an invalid output_audio_format shows the voice-gender message ('invalid text voice gender,...'): don't rely on the message text to tell the two apart.

Only 400 (character limit, language, accent, gender, format) and 503 (timeout) bodies are documented. The status and body for an invalid API key, a rate-limit hit or exhausted credits are not documented.

The public docs describe no sandbox, test key, free tier or pricing, and don't say how text-to-speech is billed: every call hits production. The account's credit balance is readable with get_credits_balance.
Rate limit: 30 requests per minute on tts/v1/generate. Responses carry rate-limit headers; Retry-After gives the delay in seconds before retrying.

spans: This endpoint only supports text less than or equal to 4096 characters
tts text character count greater than the max limit of 100 characters
The request can timeout with an http status code 503 in 120 seconds
